note: What a server sends to set a champion's tallies for the scoreboard. The header names the champion.

fields.name: keptA
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: deaths
fields.note: How many times the champion has died.

fields.name: minionKills
fields.note: How many minions it has killed, neutral ones aside.

fields.name: kills
fields.note: How many champions it has killed. Each side's kill total is the sum over its champions. Where any champion's is above zero, a client takes first blood as taken: it raises no first-blood event and adds no first-blood bonus to a kill's value after that.

fields.name: structureKills
fields.note: One kind of structure it has destroyed.

fields.name: otherStructureKills
fields.note: The other kind of structure it has destroyed.

fields.name: keptB
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: neutralKills
fields.note: How many neutral minions it has killed.

fields.name: gap
fields.note: A client takes nothing from these bytes. A server writes zero.

fields.name: keptC
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: goldTotal
fields.note: The gold it has earned in all, shown rounded down.

fields.name: keptD
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: keptE
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: keptF
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: padding
fields.note: A client takes nothing from these bytes. A server writes zero.

fields.name: keptG
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: keptH
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: keptI
fields.note: Kept with the champion; a client shows nothing of it.

fields.name: assists
fields.note: How many kills it has assisted.

revisions.note: A fixed record of the champion's tallies. A client shows kills, deaths and assists, minionKills and neutralKills together as its minion count, the two structure kills together as its building count, and goldTotal; GoldEarned adds to goldTotal between these messages.

fields.name: size
fields.note: The whole length of what follows the header, these four bytes included, as a whole 32-bit count. A mismatch has no effect, and does not limit what a client takes.

fields.name: values
fields.note: One value per tally of the match's mode, the tallies in ascending byte order of their names. An int takes 4 bytes, a float 4, a bool 1, a 64-bit int 8, and text a 16-bit length below 255 then that many bytes. Bytes left over have no effect. A nonzero count of champion kills marks first blood taken.

fields.name: values
fields.note: The figures themselves, one after another with nothing between. Which they are comes from the client's own data for the match's mode. In a classic match there are 76, in this order: assists, inhibitors destroyed, champion kills, consumables bought, double kills, experience (f32), own inhibitors lost, own nexus lost, own turrets lost, gold earned (f32), gold spent (f32), nexus destroyed, player id, the items in slots 0 to 6, items bought, killing sprees, largest critical strike (f32), largest killing spree, largest multikill, level, longest time alive (f32), magic damage dealt (f32), magic damage to champions (f32), magic damage taken (f32), minions killed, name (text), neutral monsters killed, monsters killed in the enemy's jungle, monsters killed in the side's own jungle, never entered the game, deaths, penta kills, physical damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), ping, quadra kills, sight wards bought, skin, casts of spells 1 to 4, casts of summoner spells 1 and 2, epic monsters killed, side, a teammate never entered the game, time since the last disconnection (f32), time played (f32), time disconnected (f32), total damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), total healing, crowd control dealt (f32), time dead (f32), units healed, triple kills, true damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), turrets destroyed, unreal kills, vision wards bought, wards destroyed, wards placed, away from the keyboard, away after a failed surrender, and win (text). Every one not marked otherwise is an i32; a text is a 16-bit length and that many bytes, at most 63, with nothing to end it. ARAM, First Blood and One for All leave out the two jungle counts. The tutorial also leaves out never entered the game, sight wards bought, a teammate never entered the game, crowd control dealt, the three true damage figures, vision wards bought, wards destroyed, wards placed and away after a failed surrender. Dominion and Ascension have 75, in this order: assists, champion kills, combat score (f32), consumables bought, double kills, experience (f32), gold earned (f32), gold spent (f32), player id, the items in slots 0 to 6, items bought, killing sprees, largest critical strike (f32), largest killing spree, largest multikill, level, longest time alive (f32), magic damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), minions killed, name (text), neutral monsters killed, never entered the game, node captures, node capture assists, node neutralizations, node neutralization assists, deaths, objective score (f32), penta kills, physical damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), ping, quadra kills, sight wards bought, skin, casts of spells 1 to 4, casts of summoner spells 1 and 2, side, a teammate never entered the game, team objective, time since the last disconnection (f32), time played (f32), time disconnected (f32), total damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), total healing, total score (f32), total score rank, crowd control dealt (f32), time dead (f32), units healed, triple kills, true damage dealt, to champions and taken (f32 each), unreal kills, victory points (f32), vision wards bought, away from the keyboard, away after a failed surrender, and win (text).
